summary: Feature: Symmetric mirrors two lines, two arcs or two circles about any line, a construction line or the H or V axis, as one relation that stores the two curves and no pairing of their points. Lines pair an end they share with itself and otherwise pair their ends by where they are before each edit, so either line may run either way. A mirror reverses an arc's sweep, so arcs of one direction pair each start with the other's end and arcs of opposite directions pair start with start. Circles pair their centres, and mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius. The relation lowers as point mirrors of those pairs under one tag: an end both curves share is held on the mirror, the second end pair of two arcs gives one row because their circles already mirror, and circles add one equal-radius row. There is no new equation kind. The Constrain tool and the selection offers plan it through the shared planner. Two curves of one kind and a line or an axis, picked in any order, offer Symmetric; among three lines the one construction line is the mirror, or else the line picked last. Two kinds, and pairs a mirror cannot map, are refused with the reason. The relation is stored only in this form. Point Symmetrics that already hold two lines' ends, or a centre Symmetric of two circles with their Equal radius, show as applied, and Remove removes them. A partial mirror of lines or circles is completed with what is missing, and an Equal the mirror would repeat is refused. Equal refuses a line with an arc or circle, with the reason. Marks sit on both curves and on the mirror line, and the relation list and inspection name it Symmetric curves. Trim removes a curve Symmetric with either curve it trims and lists it; Split and Extend refuse it while it names the curve.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files and agents. Installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions and controller output are not affected. The sketch graph schema gains a second Symmetric shape, { kind: 'symmetric', curveIds, lineId }. Sketches that store it do not open in 0.0.793 or earlier; the CAD format is alpha and carries no compatibility in either direction. Every relation a sketch stores today keeps its meaning and compiles to the same equations: the 0.0.788 equation baseline replays unchanged, byte for byte. Two circles with a line, picked in the Constrain tool or offered for a selection, now give the curve Symmetric, which also keeps their radii equal. Before, they gave a point Symmetric of their centres. A point and a circle still give the point form, and three lines now also offer Symmetric. A Trim of a mirrored curve now lists the curve Symmetric in removedRelationIds. An agent request that confirms an older list rejects with unconfirmed-sketch-trim-removals and names the expected IDs. The relation editor's Symmetric centers checkbox still mirrors only two circles' centres, and does not show a curve Symmetric of those circles as checked. The worker protocol stays version 7.

checklist.schema: Sketch graph schema change: the symmetric relation gains a curveIds variant, two lines, two arcs or two circles mirrored about the lineId, which names a line or @h or @v. A parse refuses it with invalid-sketch-symmetry, giving the reason, for: two kinds; an axis among the curves; a mirror that is not a line; one curve twice; two circles on one centre; two lines on the same two ends; arcs on the same three points; arcs sharing an end that their directions pair with another point; a shared end off the mirror; and a curve point at an end of the axis line that the curves do not share. Its key sorts curveIds, so either order is one relation. Lowering emits only existing rows: symmetric-midpoint, symmetric-perpendicular, point-on-line for a shared end, and difference for two circles' radii. The lowering context gains each point's position before the edit and its Coincident identity. The precision policy gains one role, mirrorPairingTieRelative (1e-9): two lines pair their ends crossed only when that is nearer to each other's mirror images, in summed squared gaps, by more than that fraction, so near ties keep start with start. No existing role changes, so CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 1. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7 with the same buffers, and the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. The post engine API remains 1 and the saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Agent operand change: set-sketch-relation accepts the curveIds form of symmetric. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints names it Symmetric curves, with its own meaning, and lists every point of both curves and the axis line's ends. The relation offers and the Constrain tool give it for two curves of one kind and a line or an axis. Trim's removedRelationIds include a curve Symmetric that names the trimmed curve; Split refuses it with dependent-sketch-split, and Extend refuses it as a dependency. Nothing new runs on pointer moves. A lowering of a curve Symmetric reads the pairing once, which for two lines compares four distances, and the planner reads a selection once.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added or removed. The symmetric agent summary names lines, arcs and circles, and the WebMCP discovery metadata stays at 51,178 of 51,200 bytes, unchanged. The public agent guide documents the curve form, its pairing, its refusals, the relations recognised as already holding it, the Equal refusals, and Trim, Split and Extend. The CAD guide documents picking, marks and refusals. Constrain offers Symmetric for two lines, two arcs or two circles and a line or an axis, in any order. Equal says why a line and an arc or circle cannot be equal.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved CAD documents parse as before; nothing is rewritten.
checklist.verification: Equation baseline: the 0.0.788 fixture replays unchanged and is not re-recorded. Every input gives the same compiled models, native answers, graph-check hashes, constraint inspection row hashes and solver attempts, byte for byte. For that, the point Symmetric keeps its recorded agent meaning; the curve form takes its own through a new optional meaningOf on relation definitions, which constraint inspection reads. New tests: cadSketchCurveSymmetry (12) covers nine scenes about the V axis, the H axis, a fixed construction line and a fixed ordinary line. The scenes are: lines; lines running opposite ways; lines sharing an end; arcs; arcs running opposite ways; arcs sharing an end, a centre, or both ends; and circles. For every scene, mirror and pick order it checks the offer and the Constrain tool step, and choosing the mirror among three lines. It also checks the prompts and the pairing, including opposite line directions, opposite arc sweeps, and the pairing tie on each side of mirrorPairingTieRelative. Lowering: one tag and one row for each freedom held, 4, 4, 3, 5, 5, 4, 4, 3 and 3, with the circle radius row. A native solve checks the reflection and the freedom left. Mirror parity: 504 configurations, each compared three ways (H, the construction line and the line against V), with every choice of fixed, expression-held and Fix-held points and a planted conflict. Every one agrees in result, reason, message, freedom, conflicting, redundant and partly redundant ids, issues and definition, across solved, redundant and conflicting outcomes. Refusals cover two kinds, one curve twice, a mirror that is not a line, an axis among the curves, circles on one centre, lines on the same two ends, arcs on the same three points, arcs sharing a start, an axis line end, and Equal of a line with an arc or circle. De-duplication and recognition: key order; applied with Remove ids; point Symmetrics of two lines applied, or half of them completed; circles with a centre Symmetric and an Equal radius, either one completed by the other; a partial arc mirror refused; an Equal the mirror repeats refused. Also covered: names and meanings, an agent edit with the curve form, Trim removing the relation from an end trim and a circle trim, and Split and Extend refusing it. Existing tests touched: the offers (three lines also offer Symmetric; two circles on one centre give the circles reason), the registry (a curve Symmetric reference), the constraint tool (the Equal and circles reasons), the glyph layout (curve marks on both curves and the mirror line, none for an axis), the offer parity rules, and the precision role pin. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry, the offer parity, both baselines, the registry, offers, symmetry relations, lowering, constraint tool and glyph layout suites (96 tests). Arcs of one direction paired start with start fails 7. Two point Symmetrics no longer counted as a line mirror fails 1. A key that keeps the curves in stored order fails 2. Circles without their equal-radius row fail 2. The equation baseline passes under each. Trim without the curve Symmetric removal fails the trim test, and a pairing tie of 0 fails the pairing test and the precision pin. Merge: main at 0.0.791 is merged, keeping 0.0.794 after 0.0.793. The pairing tie reads the new precision role to satisfy the precision literal check. Checks on the merged tree: the full Vitest suite passed, 6,966 tests in 614 files, including the equation baseline and the discovery budget. The discovery budget was measured unchanged at 51,178 bytes. npm run build (tsc -b, vite build, docs build and check) passed. Lint, with the precision literal check, has zero findings. ui:check passed. check-release passed alone; against origin/main it fails only because 0.0.792 and 0.0.793 have not merged. The e2e project type-checks. Chromium specs on the merged build, each run alone with two workers: cad-sketch-selectable-axes 7, including two lines about the V axis and two circles about a construction line, each made Symmetric from Constrain, checked as reflected with one radius and its marks, shown as applied when picked again in another order, and removed; cad-sketch-constraints 28; cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7; and cad-sketch-symmetry 1. All passed. Deferred: Coradial, Rigid set and Equal spacing. The relation editor’s Symmetric centers checkbox is left to the panel work. No benchmark was run: nothing new runs on pointer moves.

publicNotes.summary: Points, lines, arcs and circles can be made symmetric about any line or axis.
changes: Select two lines, two arcs or two circles with a line or the H or V axis, in any order, and choose Symmetric to mirror them as whole curves.
Mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius, and mirrored lines may run either way.
Symmetric marks show on both curves and on the mirror line. Choose Symmetric again with the same selection to remove it.
Equal says why a line cannot be equal to an arc or circle.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Sketches with mirrored curves do not open in older releases.
